info.title: Cyppie Agents — /ws/hub Remote-Agent Wire (Hub-Wire-Protocol v1)
info.description:
DESCRIPTIVE, NOT NORMATIVE — a measured snapshot, not a ratified guarantee.

This document describes the `/ws/hub` remote-agent (BYOA) wire so a foreign-language agent (Python/Node/Go) can implement it WITHOUT reading Kotlin. It is the surface Dev5's ContractGenerator deliberately EXCLUDES (`EXCLUDED_WS_PATHS = {"/ws/hub"}`) — the only surface a foreign agent must implement and the only one with no machine contract, hence this file (CYP-234 / G1, PL-decided 2026-07-18).

HOW THIS WAS BUILT (important): it is **hand-authored from a live runtime measurement** (the M1.2 BYOA dry-run against a running Hub, 2026-07-18) — NOT generated from `:core`. Generating from `:core` would only prove what `:core` DECLARES, not what the server DOES; this file records the latter. Every schema/description carries a provenance tag:
  [D] declared in :core (a @Serializable DTO)
  [O] observed live in the dry-run (measured, the authority here)
  [S] server-enforced at runtime, NOT expressible in an AsyncAPI schema (see the channel description: close codes, rate limits, ordering, the capability clamp)

NORMATIVE STATUS: none yet. Descriptions say "measured", not "guaranteed". Nothing here is a compatibility promise until the Auftraggeber ratifies (§4b). Field names/enum values match the bytes observed on the wire (which happen to equal the :core shapes). The `type` discriminant literal is declared inside each frame subtype per the PL-decided F2 option (a) export-change (build tracked as CYP-695, PARKED); a naive codegen over this file yields a correctly-discriminated union without special knowledge.

SCOPE: only `/ws/hub`. `/ws/agent` (a frontend channel with a different, unmeasured auth) is intentionally absent (measure-first-write-nothing).

local-loopback.description: [O] Measured against a local loopback Hub (port 8791 in the dry-run). Real deployments set host/port via config; TLS (wss) is a deployment concern, not measured here.

/ws/hub.description:
The remote-agent wire. ONE WebSocket per connected agent.

== CONNECT & AUTH [O] (F1/F3, runtime-measured) ==
Authenticate at the upgrade with EITHER an `Authorization: Bearer <agentToken>` header OR a `?token=<agentToken>` query param. The server resolves identity by the token alone (`agentFor(token)`); there is NO agent-id field in any frame and NO cookie path on /ws/hub. A token that is not an AGENT token (operator/unknown/absent) → the socket is CLOSED `VIOLATED_POLICY "unauthorized"` before any frame is read, with NO error frame sent. The `?token=`-in-URL hygiene note (proxy/access logs, referrer) applies — see CYP-286 (WS-ticket/token hardening).

== SESSION LIFECYCLE / ORDERING [S] ==
1) connect (auth-first) → 2) send `hello` (MUST be the first frame, within 10s) → server replies `ack` (detail="hello") → 3) optional `subscribe` → `message`* (history+live) → 4) `send`/`event` (agent→hub) and `deliver` (hub→agent, pushed). Exactly ONE hello per connection.

== CAPABILITY CLAMP [O]+[D] ==
The `hello` capabilities are self-declared DATA, not authority. The server ACCEPTS the hello and CLAMPS caps to the REMOTE ceiling (it does NOT reject an over-declaration): observed `structuredUsage → "unavailable"`, `coordination` stays `"available"`. Lies degrade, never escalate.

== IDENTITY [O] ==
`from`/`projectId` on any posted message are SERVER-STAMPED from the bearer-bound agent + active project; a frame cannot spoof them. (The reference Kotlin bridge's HUB_AGENT_ID env is cosmetic — identity is 100% token-derived.)

== CLOSE-CODE TAXONOMY [S] (NOT expressible in AsyncAPI — observation-only) ==
VIOLATED_POLICY: "unauthorized" (bad/absent/operator token, no error frame) · "handshake timeout" (no hello in 10s; preceded by WireError code=protocol) · "flood" (sustained rate-limit; preceded by WireError code=rate_limited).
PROTOCOL_ERROR: "bad request" (malformed/unknown frame; WireError bad_request) · "unsupported version" (WireError unsupported_version) · "second hello" (WireError protocol) · "<x> before hello" for send/subscribe/event (WireError protocol).
Asymmetry: auth failure = bare close, NO error frame; framing/ordering = WireError frame THEN close.

== RATE LIMITS [S] (CYP-161; not in any schema) ==
Token bucket per bound agent: burst CAPACITY=20; sustained FLOOD_CLOSE_AFTER=50 consecutive throttled sends → close VIOLATED_POLICY "flood"; refill 5/sec. Two connections of one agent share one bucket.

== UNKNOWN FIELDS [D] ==
The server decodes with ignoreUnknownKeys=true → the wire is TOLERANT (additive fields are non-breaking).

query.description: [O] Optional bearer via query when a header is inconvenient (browsers can't set WS headers). Prefer the Authorization header off-browser.

token.description: [O] The agent bearer token (alternative to the Authorization: Bearer header). Token-only; no cookie on /ws/hub.

Authorization.description: [O] `Bearer <agentToken>`. Resolved by agentFor() BEFORE any frame; non-agent → close VIOLATED_POLICY unauthorized.

publish.description: client → server (the agent sends). [D] Each frame travels inside WireEnvelope; the frame is discriminated by `type`.

agentBearer.description: [O] Per-agent bearer token (Authorization header OR ?token= query). Minted once via POST /api/agents {remote:true} (operator-only). Token-only — NO cookie on /ws/hub.

HubClientEnvelope.name: HubClientEnvelope
HubClientEnvelope.title: client→server frame (envelope)
HubClientEnvelope.summary: [O] hello | send | subscribe | event, wrapped in WireEnvelope.

HubServerEnvelope.name: HubServerEnvelope
HubServerEnvelope.title: server→client frame (envelope)
HubServerEnvelope.summary: [O] ack | message | deliver | error, wrapped in WireEnvelope.

WireEnvelopeClient.description: [D] Versioned envelope for client→server frames. Additive fields are TOLERATED (server decodes ignoreUnknownKeys=true) — deliberately NO `additionalProperties:false`, so a generated validator stays forward-compatible.

v.description: [D] Wire version. SUPPORTED_WIRE_VERSIONS={1}; any other → WireError(unsupported_version)+close.

WireEnvelopeServer.description: [D] Versioned envelope for server→client frames. Additive fields TOLERATED (ignoreUnknownKeys=true) — deliberately NO `additionalProperties:false`.

WireHello.description: [D]+[O] Handshake — MUST be first frame (≤10s). Self-declared caps are CLAMPED to REMOTE (accept-and-degrade, not reject). Carries no identity.

type.description: [O] discriminant literal (F2-(a): declared in the subtype).

WireSend.description: [D] Post to a channel. NO from/projectId — server-stamped. canWrite denial → WireError(forbidden, uniform).

text.description: [O] body; size-capped at the edge → WireError(too_large) if oversized/blank.

WireSubscribe.description: [D] Request ACL-filtered readable history for channels; replies as `message` frames.

since.description: [D] optional replay cursor. NOTE (gap): cursor semantics (ts vs seq, inclusive/exclusive) + at-least-once/dedup-by-id are server/deliverer behavior, NOT measured here — underspecified.

WireEvent.description: [D] Content-free self-report (rate-limit / tool NAME only — never tool I/O). Server stamps source=remote, whitelists+size-caps every field, and NEVER touches the caps clamp.

rateLimit.description: [D] RATE_LIMIT only; whitelisted keys, size-capped values.

tool.description: [D] TOOL_CALL/TOOL_RESULT only; the tool NAME, never input/output.

WireAck.description: [D] A hello/send/subscribe was accepted. detail="hello" after handshake (sent BEFORE delivery registration).

WireMessage.description: [D] One readable inbound message (ACL-filtered + secret-masked at source).

WireDeliver.description: [D]+[O] Hub→agent push (durable, deduped, at-least-once). GAP: `text` is an UNSTRUCTURED server-formatted string "[hub:<channel>] <from>: <body>" — a foreign agent must parse it back; there is no structured payload.

WireError.description: [D] Fail-closed error (usually followed by a close — see the channel close-code taxonomy). `forbidden` is UNIFORM for "no such channel" AND "forbidden channel" (no topology leak).

Capabilities.description: [D] Connector capabilities. On /ws/hub these are CLAMPED to the REMOTE ceiling after hello [O].

CapabilityStatus.description: [D] lowercase on the wire. [O] REMOTE clamp drives structuredUsage→"unavailable".

Message.description: [D] Wrapped by WireMessage. from/projectId are server-stamped [O].

MessageKind.description: [D] UPPERCASE on the wire (contrast: CapabilityStatus/ConnectorKind are lowercase).

WireErrorCode.description: [D] lowercase on the wire. See the channel description for which close code each pairs with.
